# IAM findings accepted on the RENDERED PLAN scan (deploy-infra.yml), by check ID AND
# resource. Anything not listed here fails the job when GATE_CHECKOV_PLAN=block.
#
# EMPTY, again as of 2026-11-13. Its last two entries were the static portal's deploy grant, whose
# `cloudfront:CreateDistribution` and `cloudfront:CreateResponseHeadersPolicy` cannot be scoped; the
# grant went once the Next.js server became the only front door and the portal's distribution was
# destroyed, and the two findings went with it. docs/security-baseline.md has the measurement.
#
# Every IAM finding on the plan fails the job unless it is listed here: accepted by check ID AND RESOURCE, never by
# check ID alone, so the same rule firing on any other policy still fails. The USER-FACING ISOLATION policies (`portal-role-permissions` and the
# per-plane control-plane execution roles) have zero `Resource: "*"` and must stay that way.
# That claim is narrowed deliberately: it does not cover every role in the account. The SPA's
# ECS task-execution role holds `ecr:GetAuthorizationToken` on `"*"`, which is unscopable (the
# action takes no resource type at all) and reaches no user data. Its scoped siblings — the
# three pull actions and the two log actions — name the repository and the log group.
#
# A line here that no longer matches a finding is a HARD ERROR — it either describes something
# already fixed, or points at a resource that has been renamed, in which case it is accepting
# nothing while reading as an acceptance. Delete or correct the line.
#
# This blocks PRs only. The `plan` job runs on pull_request; `apply` runs on push/dispatch and
# does not depend on it, so nothing here can redden a production deploy.
#
# ONE PIECE OF FRICTION WORTH EXPECTING. Adding a wildcard statement to
# `github_actions_deploy` — the recurring case CLAUDE.md's "Infra rule" mandates for any spec
# provisioning new infra — fires CKV_AWS_355 for any scopable action in it, CKV_AWS_290 if
# that action is also a write, and CKV_AWS_63 for `Action: "*"`. Those three are the ones that
# reach this resource. CKV_AWS_356 / CKV_AWS_111 / CKV_AWS_49 are their `aws_iam_policy_document`
# DATA-SOURCE twins and cannot fire on an `aws_iam_role_policy` — measured against the pinned
# checkov, after this file spent a release naming them. So such a change is a two-step edit:
# the grant, and the acceptance for it. Deliberate.
